transform = nuke.createNode('Transform','',False) 
transform.setInput(0, gradematcher.input(1))

transform['translate'].setValue(gradematcher['translation'].getValueAt(0),0) 
transform['scale'].setValue(gradematcher['scale'].getValueAt(0),0) 
reformat = nuke.createNode('Reformat','',False) 
reformat.setInput(0, transform) 
reformat['type'].setValue(1) 
reformat['box_width'].setValue(gradematcher['boxWidth'].getValue()) 
reformat['box_height'].setValue(gradematcher['boxHeight'].getValue()) 
reformat['box_fixed'].setValue(True) 
reformat['resize'].setValue(0) 
reformat['center'].setValue(False) 
x = gradematcher.xpos() 
y = gradematcher.ypos() 
w = gradematcher.screenWidth() 
if (gradematcher['autoCrop'].getValue()): 
  crop = nuke.createNode('Crop','',False) 
  crop['box'].setValue(gradematcher['crop'].getValueAt(0),0) 
  crop.setInput(1, reformat) 
  transform.setXYpos(x, int(y - w) ) 
  reformat.setXYpos(x, int(y - w/1.5) ) 
  crop.setXYpos(x, int(y - w/3) )

  reformat.setXYpos(x, int(y - w/3) ) 
  gradematcher.setInput(1, reformat)

Select 'Crop Target' if the target contains a region that isn't present in the source, for example a black border. If 'Crop Target' is selected, 'Align Target to Source' will also generate a rectangular crop for the target.

MatchGrade will store the transformation as a LUT. Specify the resolution of the LUT. Try 64 to improve accuracy. This could help when two very similar colors in the source image are very different in the target. Try 16 to speed up processing when the higher resolution is not needed.

Select a mask channel for MatchGrade to process. Only colors in the masked region are used to calculate the grade.

When the task is set to 'Match Graded Source', the mask is taken from the source input. Using a mask for this task can be useful for matching elements between shots. For example, match only a face region to get a good match for the skin tone.

When the task is set to 'Match Different Clip', the mask is taken from both the source and target input. Using a mask for this task can be useful for balancing the color content. For example, if the Source and Target inputs have a different amount of grass and sky, you can use a Roto node in both inputs to create masks that cover the same amount of grass and sky.

Set the match grade task.

Use 'Match Graded Source' to match the source to a graded version of the source connected to the target input. This can be used to extract a baked in grade and export the grade to use with the original source footage. The source and target pixels need to be aligned. Press 'Align Target To Source' to automatically compute the alignment.

Use 'Match Different Clip' to match the source to different footage. Use this to calculate a grade to match the look in the target footage.

See the node help for more information.
Specifies the offset of the CDL transform. The offset can either be automatically estimated or manually tuned and locked to prevent the values from being recalculated.
Specify the LUT file. This will be written in .csp format.

Select viewer output. Use 'Matched' to view the matched result. Use 'Source' to view the source input and 'Target' to view the target input. When viewing the MatchGrade node, switch between 'Source' and 'Target' to set keys at reference frames.
Specifies the power of the CDL transform. The power can either be automatically estimated or manually tuned and locked to prevent the values from being recalculated.
Specify the 1D shaper LUT to use for the analysis. Select 'AutoDetect' to automatically detect the best pre LUT.

Specifies the slope of the CDL transform. The slope can either be automatically estimated or manually tuned and locked to prevent the values from being recalculated.

The keyed reference frames selected for the source footage. Choose frames that cover the characteristic colors in the source sequence. When the task is set to 'Match Graded Source' the same frames are used for both the source and target inputs.

The keyed reference frames for the target footage. When the task is set to 'Match Different Clip' you will need to key separate sets of frames for the source and target inputs. Make sure that the selected frames cover similar content in both source and target sequences, for example, same amount of grass, skin etc. . There is no need to use the same number of keyed frames and there is no need to key the same frame on source and target.
Specify the transformation that is used to grade the source input. Note that the CDL transform is limited and may not always fit the data well.

description.plain_text: MatchGrade Use MatchGrade to automatically calculate a grade to match source to target footage. Match Graded Source: MatchGrade can be used to extract a baked-in grade by matching the source footage with a graded version of the source. Use this to create and export the grade to use with the original source footage. The same frames are expected on the source and target inputs and the source and target pixels need to be aligned. Press 'Auto Align Target to Source' to automatically compute the alignment. Match Different Clip: MatchGrade can also be used to match the grade in a different clip where the source and target frames are different. Use this to create a grade to reproduce the look of the target in the source footage. You can for example create the grade to match an element between different shots by using the mask input to match the colors on the element only in the different clips. Analyze Reference Frames: The grade is calculated by analysing a set of reference frames. First set the matching task then key reference frames that pick out the characteristic colors in each sequence. Finally, press 'Analyze Reference Frames' to calculate the grade. Export: The grade can be exported in .csp format for use with the OCIO FileTransform node. A CDL transform can also be calculated and exported to OCIO CDLTransform. There is the option to manually set CDL parameters and recalculate the best fit transform. Auto-analyze Per Frame: You can calculate the best grade to use on a frame-by-frame basis when extracting a baked in grade. Select 'Auto-analyze per frame' when the task is set to 'Match Graded Source' to enable this.
description.text:
MatchGrade

Use MatchGrade to automatically calculate a grade to match source to target footage.

Match Graded Source:

MatchGrade can be used to extract a baked-in grade by matching the source footage with a graded version of the source. Use this to create and export the grade to use with the original source footage. The same frames are expected on the source and target inputs and the source and target pixels need to be aligned. Press 'Auto Align Target to Source' to automatically compute the alignment.

Match Different Clip:

MatchGrade can also be used to match the grade in a different clip where the source and target frames are different. Use this to create a grade to reproduce the look of the target in the source footage. You can for example create the grade to match an element between different shots by using the mask input to match the colors on the element only in the different clips.

Analyze Reference Frames:

The grade is calculated by analysing a set of reference frames. First set the matching task then key reference frames that pick out the characteristic colors in each sequence. Finally, press 'Analyze Reference Frames' to calculate the grade.

Export:

The grade can be exported in .csp format for use with the OCIO FileTransform node. A CDL transform can also be calculated and exported to OCIO CDLTransform. There is the option to manually set CDL parameters and recalculate the best fit transform.

Auto-analyze Per Frame:

You can calculate the best grade to use on a frame-by-frame basis when extracting a baked in grade. Select 'Auto-analyze per frame' when the task is set to 'Match Graded Source' to enable this.
